newsitem.title: UK: S&P may cut Hertz credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P may cut Hertz credit ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it had placed on CreditWatch with negative implications Hertz Corp's A corporate credit and senior unsecured debt ratings, A minus subordinated debt rating, and A1 commercial paper rating.
It said in a statement that about $2.5 billion of rated debt was affected.
The rating actions reflect the announcement made by Hertz's 100 percent owner, Ford Motor Co. (A plus corporate credit rating), that it is reviewing strategic options for its investment in Hertz.

The ratings of Hertz, the world's largest car rental company, have incorporated Ford's 100 percent ownership, as well as its strategic importance as Ford's largest customer. With Ford's recent de-emphasis on fleet sales, its ultimate ownership and support of Hertz have become less certain, S&P said.
"If less support were to be provided by Ford in the future, Hertz's ratings likely would fall within the BBB category. The ratings of Ford and other related entities are not affected", S&P said.

Hertz participates in the business and leisure rental segment of the business, which is fiercely price competitive and typically has produced poor margins, or even losses, for all participants in this sector, even during healthy economic periods.

While Hertz's earnings have been relatively strong since 1994, its debt leverage is in the mid-80 percentrange, which is high for a transportation equipment lessor. However, Hertz does have relatively strong financial flexibility, in large part due to the highly liquid nature of the assets, and this is likely to continue going forward, even with a reduced Ford ownership stake.
